## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sadhāyamāna Sutta* is the ninth discourse of the fifth chapter (*Soṇavagga*) of the *Udāna* (PTS Ud 61) [Masefield 1997; SuttaCentral]. In this sutta, a group of youths jeers at the monks [SuttaCentral]. In his translation notes, Peter Masefield observes textual variants for the text, adopting the reading *sadhāyamānā* with the Siamese edition (*Se*, alongside the Burmese reading *sadhāya*) in place of the Pali Text Society reading *saddāyamānā* [Masefield 1997]. SuttaCentral records sixteen translations across thirteen modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies verse parallels in the Sanskrit and Tibetan versions of the *Udānavarga* (UV 14 *Drohavarga* and Uv Kg 14 *Hatred*), as well as thematic and verse parallels in other Pali works, including the *Upakkilesa Sutta* (MN 128), the *Kosambiyajātaka* (Ja 428), and the Vinaya *Kosambakakkhandhaka* (Kd 10) [SuttaCentral]. In addition, automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus detects Pali-internal shared formulaic passages between this sutta and the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16), the *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5), and the *Tikanipāta* (AN 3) [DharmaNexus].
